newsitem.title: USA: US FCC chief criticizes proposed digital TV std.
newsitem.headline: US FCC chief criticizes proposed digital TV std.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission reiterated criticism Friday for his agency's proposed digital television (DTV) standard, but did not altogether rule out such a standard.
""Virtually every industry needs standards and manages on its own to set them," Reed Hundt told a radio and TV industry group in New York.
"Under certain circumstances, we should consider blessing a DTV stndard by embodying it in an FCC rule. I doubt this is necessary, but I'm not dead set against it."

Hundt repeated that any FCC standard for DTV -- which promises cinema-quality pictures and sound -- should "at minimum" have a "sunset provision" under which the standard would expire after a certain time.
He also said any standard should:
-- Be compatible with the business strategies of both DTV manufacturers and computer hardware and software companies.
-- Be capable of evolving over time as compression technology and other enhancements are developed.
-- And be cost-effective both for broadcasters to transmit and consumers to receive voice, video and data.
